gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Epson CO-FH02 has only one video input ('1 x HDMI'), that Epson's own guide puts the Android TV streaming player on that same HDMI port inside a covered side compartment (so plugging in a laptop means opening the cover and unplugging the player, and the projector's wireless works only through that player on a Wi-Fi network of 5 Mbps or more), or that the CO-W01 also has one HDMI port and gets wireless only from an optional ELPAP11 module.
standout_why: I compared against beecommercer (cited, 2026-11-08). It already says 'The included streaming player occupies the HDMI path' for the CO-FH02, and that the Capsule 3 Laser's USB-C 'is not a verified laptop video input'. It does not give the port count, the covered compartment, the 5 Mbps network requirement for casting, that the CO-W01's wireless is an optional add-on, or any power-draw figure. It lists Chromecast, power-bank operation and USB display as unaddressed. ChatGPT's answer already says the Epsons need an outlet, so the 270 W figure only adds the number. rottenwifi (cited) timed out on both tries, so I could not check it. The other top results were not opened.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's Epson picks but adds a condition. With the CO-FH02 or CO-W01, the presenter must carry an HDMI cable, plus a USB-C-to-HDMI adapter for laptops that only have USB-C, because there is no USB-C video input and no wireless built into the projector. The CO-FH02 can cast wirelessly only after its streaming player joins a Wi-Fi network of 5 Mbps or more. Both draw 270 W, so outlet-free use needs an AC power station that can supply more than 270 W continuously, not a USB-C power bank. A shopper who wants one-cable USB-C or reliable wireless should look at models with USB-C DisplayPort input, which beecommercer names (BenQ GV50, ASUS ZenBeam L2), rather than the CO-FH02.

findings.label: Video inputs
findings.value: 1 x HDMI. Also 1 x USB A ('For power supply, firmware update, copy OSD settings') and 1 x USB B ('For firmware update, copy OSD settings'). No USB video input.
findings.source_title: Epson New Zealand – CO-FH02 product page
findings.note: Maker's New Zealand page. Epson's US product page does not give the port count. Retailers B&H and Micro Center also list one HDMI (seen in search results only, not opened).

findings.label: Where the Android TV player plugs in
findings.value: 'You can connect the Epson streaming media player for Android TV to the projector's HDMI port… Connect the HDMI extension cable to the HDMI port and the USB power cable to the DC Out port… fit it into the port compartment… Replace the side cover.'
findings.source_title: Epson CO-FH02 User's Guide – Connecting to a Streaming Media Player
findings.note: Combined with '1 x HDMI', this means the player and a laptop cable use the same port. This guide page does not itself describe swapping them.

findings.label: Wireless and casting path
findings.value: Chromecast is listed as 'Included' and works from 'popular Android and Apple devices' (may require additional software). Android TV and streaming need a 'wireless network connection of 5 Mbps or faster'. The box includes a 'Mini-USB cable for Android TV power'. Price shown: $499.99.
findings.source_title: Epson US – EpiqVision Flex CO-FH02 Full HD 1080p Smart Portable Projector
findings.note: Epson New Zealand lists wireless as 'Included (via SMP)', meaning through the streaming media player, not built into the projector.

findings.label: Power consumption
findings.source_title: Epson New Zealand – CO-FH02 product page
findings.note: The page lists 270 W under the light source. Search results quoted the Epson America spec sheet at 284 W normal / 223 W ECO, but that PDF returned 403 so I left those numbers out. 270 W is far above what a USB-C power bank supplies, so running without an outlet needs an AC power station rated above 270 W continuous.

findings.label: Weight / brightness / keystone
findings.value: 2.6 kg; 3,000 lumens colour and white; ±30° vertical and horizontal keystone
findings.source_title: Epson New Zealand – CO-FH02 product page
findings.note: Epson's US page states '3,000 lumens of color brightness (IDMS Rated) and 3,000 lumens of white brightness (ISO Rated)'.

findings.label: Inputs and wireless
findings.value: 1 x HDMI. 1 x USB A ('For Wireless LAN, firmware update, copy OSD settings'). 1 x USB B (firmware and OSD only). Wireless: 'Optional (ELPAP11)'.
findings.source_title: Epson New Zealand – CO-W01 product page
findings.note: With no add-on, the only way to connect is one HDMI cable. There is no USB-C video input.

findings.source_title: Epson New Zealand – CO-W01 product page
